PUBLIC NOTICE

Inviting further submission on Plan Change 5 (District Boundary Change matters)

Kawerau District Council give notice that the summary of submissions has been prepared for Proposed Plan Change 5 (District Boundary Change matters) and that further submissions are now invited until 23 July 2026, under Clause 7, Schedule 1 of the Resource Management Act 1991. 
 
The Proposed Plan Change 5 - (District Boundary Change matters) incorporates:

  • Zoning of land transferred to Kawerau District (as part of the boundary Re-organisation in September 2024)
  • Updated Significant Natural Areas (previously known as Natural Heritage Sites/Areas)
  • Introduction of a (new) Māori Purpose Zone 

All other provisions remain unchanged.

Summary of Submissions

The Council received 2 submissions on Plan Change 5.  A summary has been prepared and is available for inspection at the Kawerau District Council Office, Library and online.

Making a Further Submission

A further submission is limited to only expressing support or opposition to a matter raised in an original submission.  It must not raise new points.

A further submission may only be made by: 

  • a person representing a relevant aspect of the public interest; or 
  • a person who has an interest in Proposed Plan Change 5 greater than the interest of the general public.

Further submissions must be in writing on the form provided and state whether you wish to speak to your submission.  A form is available online here.

A copy of your submission is also required to be sent to the original submitter not later than 5 working days after lodging your further submission to the Kawerau District Council (Clause 8A, Schedule 1 RMA). The address for service is available with the summary of submissions.

Submissions close on 5pm on Thursday 23 July 2026.  

After the close of further submissions:

  • A hearing will be held to consider submissions and further submissions; 
  • The Council will make and publicly notify its decision on Plan Change 5; and 
  • Council decisions may be appealed to the Environment Court.

For further information, please contact Council on 07 3069009 

The Draft Kawerau District Plan Change 5, addresses the necessary updates to the Kawerau District Plan following the April 2024 boundary reorganisation that transferred land from the Whakatāne District to the Kawerau District.

Council is legally required to rezone this newly acquired land by September 2026 and to include Significant Natural Areas (SNAs) from the Whakatāne District Plan affected by the boundary change. Although the Government issued a "plan stop" directive in August 2025, Kawerau District Council successfully applied for an exemption to continue this work, which was approved in December 2025.

The scope of the District Plan Change 5 review is limited to re-zoning land transferred in the boundary reorganisation; a new Māori purpose zone and recognising the significant nature areas that come into the Kawerau District from Whakatāne. Conversations and consultation has been carried out with the registered land owners of all the land parcels which were part of the boundary reorganisation. This includes consultation with Ngati Tuwharetoa (Bay of Plenty) Settlement Trust on the Māori purpose zone. The purpose of the early engagement with those involved with the boundary reorganisation was to ensure that the goals and aspirations for their land were incorporated into the rezoning of the draft Māori purpose zone. Further consultation with landowners has been undertaken through the upcoming formal consulation period which is also open for the community from Friday, 27 March to 30 April 2026. Following this process, Council adopted the Proposed Kawerau District Plan Change 5 on Wednesday 3 June 2026 for consultation. The formal consultation period will run from 5 June 2026 to 5 July 2026 for the community to make a submission (please see below for how to make a submission).

Māori Purpose Zone

The Kawerau District contains a significant area of Māori ancestral land and Treaty settlement land. It is recognised that this legal and governance framework for Māori land provides for a unique situation for tangata whenua. 

The Māori Purpose Zone recognises and provides for the relationship of Māori with:

  • Māori customary land or Māori freehold land as defined in the Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993;
  • Treaty Settlement Land including Cultural and Commercial redress land owned by iwi or hapu through Treaty Claims Settlement legislation;
  • Land held by or on behalf of an iwi or hapū if the land was transferred from the Crown, a Crown body, or a local authority with the intention of returning the land to the holders of the tangata whenua over the land; and
  • Land held by a Post-Settlement Governance Entity (PSGE) for the long-term benefit of iwi members.

The zone provides for the use and development of Māori land which can support the social, cultural and economic aspirations of tangata whenua and enable a range of cultural and economic activities to be undertaken. Council has responsibilities under Te Tiriti o Waitangi and Te Ture Whenua Māori Act to provide for the on-going use and development of Māori land.

The zone permits a wide range of activities including: 

  • Māori Purpose Activities 
  • Commercial 
  • Agriculture, horticulture, green houses
  • Conservation and recreation 
  • Small scale renewable electricity generation activities 

The National Environmental Standards (NES) in New Zealand are regulations made under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA) that set consistent rules for environmental matters across the country. The National Environmental Standards for Papakainga (NES-P) contains regulations (rules) for papakāinga and some ancillary activities. Those regulations apply in the Māori Purpose Zone. [NOTE – the NES-P is to be released in 2026]
Owners and Trustees of Māori land can use the provisions of the NES-P and Māori Purpose Zone as relevant to proposed use and development. Activities are governed are governed by rules of the zone which include, but are not limited to: 

  • Height in relation to boundary (refer diagram below)
  • Setbacks - from road and side/rear boundaries 
  • Greater distances where adjoining Residential Zones
  • Site coverage - 50%  
  • Noise levels 

 

Significant Natural Areas 

The District Plan has been prepared to list the Significant Natural Areas, previously referred to as Natural Heritage Sites. This will include areas already in the Kawerau District and incorporate the four areas that have been transferred with land from the Whakatāne District. (Refer to the map showing the locations of all Significant Natural Areas). 

Existing significant natural areas in District Plan and significant natural areas from Whakatane District brought in through boundary adjustment. No new significant natural areas. 

Proposed Plan Change 5 Process

The Council formally adopted the Proposed Plan Change 5 for public notification on Wednesday, 3 June 2026. This is the formal process required under Resource Management Act (RMA) for submissions and hearing, Landowners impacted by Plan Change 5, and the public may only make submissions on the matters being changed in the District Plan. 

Provide Feedback via a formal submission 

Council is seeking your opinion on Proposed Plan Change 5 which includes rezoning of the land blocks transferred into Kawerau District from the boundary reorganisation, a (new) draft Māori Purpose Zone chapter and the updated significant natural areas (formerly natural heritage site). Any person or organisation is welcome to provide feedback on Proposed Plan Change 5.

The consultation period for submissions opens on Friday 5 June and closes on Sunday 5 July..

The Council has completed pre-engagement with those directly affected, and also gathered feedback from the wider community. This feedback has been considered and the Proposed Plan Change 5 was approved by Council on Wednesday, 3 June 2026 at the Exrtraordinary Meeting for public notification and formal submissions. The submission period is from 5 June to 5 July 2026.

After the submission period closes, Council will prepare and publicly notify the availability of a summary of submissions and where they can be inspected. Further submissions in support, or in opposition to, the submissions already made can then be made by any person representing a relevant public interest, has an interest greater than the general public or the local authority. Those who make a submission will have an opportunity to be heard at a hearing. Decisions on the matters raised in the submission will be notified publicly and served on all submitters after the public hearing and within two years of the proposal being notified. 

Hard copy submission forms are available in the Kawerau District Council Offices and Kawerau District Library

Please note Kawerau District Council must receive submissions by 5.00pm on Sunday 5 July 2026.
If you would like to talk directly to our planner regarding the Proposed District Plan Change 5, please contact Council on 07 306 9009.
